reason: The source has substantial geometric/speed information, but cross-dataset road matching remains a large unresolved research step. Using native OSM geometry/node identities directly could remove that dependency; this is an architecture hypothesis, not proven accuracy, national footprint or deployability.

recommendedFirstScope.input: Only existing complete captured JSONL for all original21validation areas and qualified cached tools. No new PBF pass/download/provider/DB access or selected-route exceptions.
recommendedFirstScope.implementation: Build native node-ID road graph and a compact degree-two contraction prototype with raw-way/node/metadata lineage and explicit boundary/unknown access/direction/structure/restriction context. Preserve junctions and every relevant metadata/barrier/restriction boundary; do not invent coordinate joins.
recommendedFirstScope.semantics: First measure topology/geometry/footprint, with separate explicit coarse car-cost/direction/access policy freeze before ETA evaluation. Missing/scoped speed limits stay visible; any later generic class fallback is a declared estimate, not inferred legal permission.
recommendedFirstScope.bounds: Keep overall4GiBzero swap/four-hour/64GiBretained work, reserve all prior closed allocations; propose<=256MiBnew owned/64MiBtmp for this small prototype and freeze exact caps/controller before execution.
acceptance: Synthetic and independent raw-versus-contracted native-ID reachability/geometry/length invariants, source/raw seals and every original-area denominator reconcile.
Measure actual prototype raw/packed/decoded bytes and operations; do not extrapolate21areas as nationwide proof.
If promising, propose a separate bounded nationwide count/footprint/input plan before country graph construction; no national-source replay in the first prototype.

Keep deployed v9. Any active model still needs independently measured national coverage/physical/source/path checks, original83/35accuracy gates,<=70MBfunction,decoded<=162238546bytes,firstpackagedestimate<=5s,software/API/shared-camera review.
